title: K Closest Points to Origin

statement.hi: Points ka array `points` (`points[i] = [x, y]`) aur integer `k` diya hai. Origin `(0, 0)` ke **k sabse kareeb** points return karo (Euclidean distance). Answer kisi bhi order me ho sakta hai. Distance barabar ho to **chhota `x`**, phir **chhota `y`** wala point pehle chuno — isse answer unique rehta hai.
statement.en: Given an array `points` where `points[i] = [x, y]` and an integer `k`, return the **k closest** points to the origin `(0, 0)` (Euclidean distance). You may return them in any order. On equal distance, prefer the point with the **smaller `x`**, then the **smaller `y`** — this keeps the answer unique.

constraints: Ties are broken by (distance, x, y)

hi: `sqrt` ki zarurat nahi — `x² + y²` compare karo.
Size `k` ka max-heap rakho, key `(dist, x, y)`; bada ho jaaye to top pop karo.
en: Keep a max-heap of size `k` keyed by `(dist, x, y)`; pop the top when it grows past `k`.

explain.en: Squared distance of (1,3) is 10 and of (-2,2) is 8, so [-2,2].

approach.hi: Har point ki key `(x² + y², x, y)` banao. Size `k` ka max-heap rakho: push karo, size `k` se zyada ho to top (sabse door) pop karo. Bache `k` points answer hain. O(n log k) time, O(k) space.
approach.en: Give each point the key `(x² + y², x, y)`. Keep a max-heap of size `k`: push each point and pop the top (the farthest) when the size exceeds `k`. The `k` points left are the answer. O(n log k) time, O(k) space.
